ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, point D is the midpoint of $BC$, point E is on $AC$, $AD=AE$, if $\angle BAD=50^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle CED$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB=AC$ and point D is the midpoint of $BC$, \\
it follows that triangle $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle, making $AD$ a median of $BC$ and the bisector of $\angle BAC$, hence $\angle CAD=\angle BAD=50^\circ$, \\
Since $AD=AE$, \\
it follows that $\angle ADE=\angle AED$, \\
Since $\angle ADE+\angle AED+\angle CAD=180^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle ADE=\angle AED=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-50^\circ)=65^\circ$, \\
Therefore, $\angle CED=180^\circ-65^\circ=\boxed{115^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right; B, D, C are on the same straight line and D is located on BC; line segment AD is drawn from A to D; point E is on side AC, and D and E are connected, so EC is the part of the line on which AE lies after E toward C. Reasoning: From the given conditions AB=AC and D is the midpoint of BC, in isosceles triangle ABC, AD is the median to the base BC and also the angle bisector of the vertex angle ∠BAC, so ∠CAD=∠BAD=50°. Because E is on AC, ∠DAE=∠DAC=50°. In triangle ADE, AD=AE, therefore the base angles ∠ADE=∠AED. Thus ∠ADE=∠AED=(180°-50°)/2=65°. Also because A, E, C are collinear, ∠CED and ∠AED are adjacent supplementary angles, so ∠CED=180°-65°=115°.
